pages.text: "I'll be first off!" Bami reached the door before Pipi called the station. The train was still stopping, but Bami pushed the door. By the yellow line, a fox painter painted a yellow maple.
Thump! Bami jumped off before the train stopped. "Faster is more fun! A platform is perfect for running!" Bami raced along the yellow line. Dad shouted from the cab, "Don't run!"
A paint box was underfoot. Bami stumbled, barely stopping at the platform's edge. Yellow paint splashed onto their scarf. Their heart pounded. They had nearly fallen onto the tracks.
Dad hurried down. "Are you okay? Going too fast keeps you from seeing ahead." Bami nodded. "I didn't see the box at all..." The fox sighed, brush in hand. "My yellow paint..."
Dad tapped the yellow line. "Stay on the safe side, away from the tracks. And walk like an owl. Owls fly quietly and softly." Bami's eyes widened. "Softly?"
"One, wait until the train stops completely! Two, stay behind the yellow line! Three, walk softly on the platform!" Dad tapped again. Bami took a quiet step. "Walk softly!"
At the next station, Bami waited for a full stop before opening the door. Behind the yellow line, step by quiet step, wings wide like a silently flying owl. "Walk softly on the platform!"

The fox had boarded with the paint box and now brushed at a window seat. "Hold still, little conductor!" A picture showed Bami walking behind the yellow line. Bami rose on tiptoe. "No falls, and I can see every paint box!"
Now Bami kept the promises at every station. "One, a full stop first! Two, behind the yellow line! Three, walk softly!" At the next station, Bami called the words before Pipi.
At the last stop, Dad touched his beak to Bami's head. "Soft steps got you there best!" Being safe was much more fun than being fast. Walk softly on the platform!
